headline: Approved a 7-2 resolution opposing revisions that remove 17 high school classrooms and a settlement in a 35 Thorpe Avenue tax appeal.
summary: Tax refunds, police donations, and budget transfers passed on the consent agenda. Softball field #1 at Pragemann Park was named for Stanley Shepardson, 9-0, after a trust question was raised about keeping the park's name. Speakers also raised the Pragemann Pavilion storage shed, sidewalks, crosswalk signs, and flock cameras.
decisions: Approved consent items 3a–3d, 3f and 3g, including tax refunds and police donations, by voice vote.
Approved naming softball field #1 at Pragemann Park after Stanley Shepardson, 9-0.
Approved, 7-2, a resolution opposing revisions that eliminate 17 high school classrooms, as amended.
Approved settlement of the pending tax appeal of 35 Thorpe Avenue Associates, LLC, 9-0.

  4. Items Removed from the Consent Agenda 
 
 5. PUBLIC QUESTION & ANSWER PERIOD 
 
Larry Kellogg addressed the Council to ask for money to be budgeted to purchase signage for 
crosswalks, specifically at schools.  Chairman Testa advised Mr. Kellogg to send a written request to the 
administration.  Chief Ventura of Wallingford Police Dept is in favor of the signs but needs to identify 
which crosswalks would be appropriate and allocate funds for the signage in the next budget. 
 
Keith Massamino followed up with a question from a previous meeting, as to why the Parks and 
Recreation Director is signing off on change-orders.  Mayor responded that Parks and Recreation is in 
charge of that project and has the authority to sign off but not it’s not without consultation from other 
appropriate professionals.  
 
Bill Comerford asked about painting in Town Hall hallways in 2024 and again in 2026.  He inquired as 
to if the issue that caused the paint to peel had been resolved.  Chairman Testa responded that he will 
look into the issue. 
 
Christine Coleman asked about flock cameras in Wallingford.  Mayor responded that “flock” is a brand 
name, such as calling a tissue a Kleenex.  Wallingford does not have flock cameras but has discussed 
cameras to enforce speeding and traffic signal enforcement.  There is a state statue that governs their 
adoption.  If Wallingford were to go forward, the issue would need to go before Town Council. 
 
Jason Michael inquired about removing items from the consent agenda and if an amended agenda should 
be issued.  Chairman Testa answered that these procedures are something the Council is looking to 
discuss.  He also asked for a final number for the cost of the Police Station.  Mayor indicated this topic 
will be put on a future agenda and addressed.  Mr. Michaels also commented on the tone of which the 
public is addressed and asked that all members of the public be treated equally. 
 
Sheila Tierney asked for an update on sidewalks.  Chairman Testa responded that he has requested an 
agenda item for the next meeting to have a lengthy discussion with the Engineering, Public Works and 
Finance Departments on the sidewalk program and road paving program.  Ms. Tierney also expressed 
concern over public vehicles using the parade ground driveway and asked for signage to be put up to 
indicate “Town Vehicles Only”.  Chairman Testa asked the Mayor to review.

 6. Chairman’s Update 
 a.  Golden Fox Theatre 
 
Joey Abate, co-founder of Golden Fox Theater made a statement regarding the impact on him and 
Golden Fox Theatre, not yet receiving the $5000 non-profit grant funds.  Mayor stated he has never 
denied the funds but needs a budget in order to release them. 
 
7.        Consider and approve the naming of softball field #1 at Pragemann Park after Stanley Shepardson   
           - Parks and Recreation  
 
Kenny Michaels, Director of Parks and Recreation addressed the Council to ask to name softball field #1 
after Stanley Shepardson, the first Recreation Director, serving 28 years in the Town of Wallingford.  
Mr. Shepardson’s children were in attendance to support their father’s service and the dedication to him. 
Councilor Fishbein and Councilor Rivard spoke in favor of the dedication.  
 
Attorney Einhorn added that there was an opinion filed in the Law Department, created by then 
Corporate Counsel Adam Mantzaris in 2001, pertaining to the naming of one of the fields at Pragemann 
Park.  There is a Will from Mr. and Mrs. Pragemann with two testamentary trusts, to contribute to the 
upkeep of the park, in the amount of $20,000 per year.  The Will states that the name of the park should 
not be changed from Pragemann Park. The opinion at the time was that the naming of the field could 
affect the funds coming from the trust.  However, no issue was ever brought up since the naming of the 
Doyle Field in 2016.  Councilor Fishbein and Councilor Tatta expressed dissatisfaction in not having 
this information prior to the meeting. 
 
Keith Massamino asked about his request to ask a question to Mr. Michaels regarding the pavilion at 
Pragemann Park.  Chairman Testa stated it was not on the Agenda but to wait until agenda item #7 is 
completed and he will address it.

Kenny Michaels, Director of Parks and Recreation explained that the Pavilion is an ongoing project, 
started in 2018, in discussion with the Wallingford Vikings Youth Football League and the Wallingford 
Youth Lacrosse Team, looking for storage spaces.  The Pragemann Pavilion has seen a decline in rentals 
since 2017.  Construction for the storage shed was to begin between 2019 – 2020 but was delayed by 
COVID.  The conversation was revisited by both leagues in 2024 and Parks and Recreation felt it was 
the right time to start the project again.  The project converted the pavilion to a storage shed and was 
funded by the Pragemann endowment fund. This will provide leagues a viable storage facility at what 
would be considered their home location. 
 
Keith Massamino asked if repairs and installs at the park require authorization from the town or 
administration.  Mr. Michaels explained that as long as it’s not a capital project and he has the funding 
in his budget, he can move forward, following the proper purchasing procedures. 
 
Chris Cirri, President of Wallingford Youth Football spoke in support of the storage shed, explaining 
that teams use the shed to house expensive equipment that keeps our children safe.  He questions why 
we spend so much time criticizing improvements in our community instead of embracing them.

Councilor Tatta questioned why we couldn’t have the Pavilion and a storage shed.  She feels we have 
taken a space that all residents can use and have turned it into a free storage space for nonprofits.  Mr. 
Michaels reiterated that reservations of the Pavilion had been declining since 2017.  Chairman Testa 
stated he would like to see a discussion about the long-term plans of the Parks and Recreation

8.        Discussion and possible action on a Resolution of the Town Council regarding the educational 
 specifications for the proposed new high school – Chairman Testa and Councilors Carmody,  
            Reynolds, Rivard, and Rossacci 
 
Town of Wallingford Town Council resolution concerning revisions to the educational specifications for 
the proposed high school consolidation project.  
 
Whereas the Wallingford Town Council recognizes the significance of the proposed high school 
consolidation project and its lasting impact on the students, educators, families, and taxpayers of the 
town of Wallingford. 
 
And whereas the educational specifications for the proposed project were developed through a process 
involving substantial public input including recommendations and advocacy from teachers, school staff, 
parents, students, and members of the community. 
 
And whereas the inclusion of 17 additional classrooms was strongly advocated for by teachers and 
school staff to provide each teacher with a dedicated classroom and to ensure an educational 
environment that best supports effective instruction, student learning and the daily operations of the 
school.  
 
And whereas teachers and school staff, whose professional experience and firsthand understanding of 
classroom needs are essential to the planning of educational facilities have consistently emphasized the 
importance of these additional classrooms.  
 
And whereas the inclusion of these 17 classrooms received support from a majority of the Board of 
Education at various stages of its deliberations and decision-making process.  
 
And whereas the town council is concerned that the subsequent revisions to the educational 
specifications eliminating the 17 classrooms represent a significant departure from the priorities 
established through public participation and the educational needs identified by teachers and school 
staff. 
 
And whereas the town council firmly believes that should the town proceed with the consolidation of its 
two high schools, the resulting facilities must reflect the highest standards of educational excellence and 
provide the best possible learning environment for current and future generations of Wallingford 
students.  
 
Now therefore, it be resolved that the Wallingford Town Council hereby formally expresses 
its opposition to the revisions to the educational specifications eliminating the 17 additional classrooms.
Wallingford, Connecticut                                                                                                                             
November 10, 2026 
Town Council Meeting                                                                                                                                                                                     Record of Votes and 
Minutes 
 
Wallingford Town Hall, 45 South Main Street 
 
6
 
And be it further resolved that the town council strongly urges the Wallingford Board of Education to 
reconsider and reverse its decision and restore these classrooms to the educational specifications 
consistent with the recommendation of teachers, school staff, parents, students, and the substantial 
public input received throughout the planning process.  
 
And be it further resolved that the town council affirms its commitment to ensuring that any 
consolidation of the town's two high schools represents a responsible forward-looking investment in 
public education and provides the highest quality educational facilities reasonably achievable for the 
benefit of generations to come.  
 
Be it finally resolved that a copy of this resolution be transmitted to the Wallingford Board of Education 
for its formal consideration adopted by the Wallingford Town Council this 10th day of November, 2026.  
 
Councilor Rossacci spoke in support of the Resolution and feels the Board of Education should 
reconsider eliminating the 17 additional classrooms.   
 
Councilor Fishbein clarified that the Board of Education is a creature of the State of Connecticut.  The 
only connection to the Town of Wallingford is the budget.  We are essentially asking a state body to 
reconsider something that is already voted on.  He feels the teachers provided input and the teachers 
should be heard. If we are going to spend $400 million on a new high school, we should have the best 
high school available.   He offered some revisions to the Resolution. 
 
A question was asked how the Resolution was created.  Chairman Testa explained it was a caucus of the 
Democrats, having a discussion and jointly putting this item on the agenda.  Councilor Tatta asked a 
question about what documentation can be requested under the Freedom Of Information Act.  Attorney 
Small explained that communications regarding the Resolution could be requested under the Freedom of 
Information Act. Councilor Tatta stated she would like to have been included on the final draft of the 
resolution.  She is also concerned about the Board of Education re-voting on this issue and how the 
votes changed through the process.  She would like to know the reasons for the change. 
 
Councilor Reynolds spoke in support of the Resolution and feels we should not be making any changes 
to size or shape while we are in the process of negotiating to buy property.  We need to support our 
educators and plan smarter, think long term and think success. 
 
Councilor Rivard believes the best people to make the assessment for the schools are the professionals 
that work in them and supports the teachers getting the 17 classrooms.  If we are to move forward with 
this project we should do it right. 
 
Councilor Laffin explained that the 17 classrooms and the pool could affect our reimbursement rate.  He 
feels we should go to the State of Connecticut to lobby for that reimbursement to be covered.  He would 
like a real vote and this Resolution will not do anything to resolve the situation.  This is a Board decision 
and we need to follow the system the way is it designed.
Wallingford, Connecticut                                                                                                                             
November 10, 2026 
Town Council Meeting                                                                                                                                                                                     Record of Votes and 
Minutes 
 
Wallingford Town Hall, 45 South Main Street 
 
7
 
Councilor Fishbein commented that before we can go to the State of Connecticut we need to find a site 
for the school. 
 
Chairman Testa feels the Board of Education made their decision to change the educational 
specifications based on a memo from the Mayor.  Mayor added that there is a possibility there are 
enough votes on Council to move forward with the project.  There is talk about the Council supporting a 
referendum for it.  If it goes to referendum and you get enough participation and positive votes, the 
project will move forward.  These are all variables.  Other variables include getting our legislative 
delegation to increase the reimbursement rate.  If we build the right size building, per pupil and square 
footage, the State of Connecticut could reimburse 52.5%.  The building we are trying to potentially build 
is looking at a reimbursement rate of 42.5%.  He feels we should absolutely be going to the State for 
more money but we cannot count on the certainty in the outcome.  He is hoping to get the most 
competitive 30-year term rate possible. 
 
Maureen Reed, Board of Education member spoke in support of the 17 classrooms.   She asked the 
Council to remember that every decision made in education should be about the kids.  She feels the 
Town Council needs to understand every aspect of the project as Council ultimately makes the decision 
about the land purchase and project. 
 
MOTION WAS MADE TO approve a Resolution of the Town Council regarding the educational 
specifications for the proposed new high school as amended.

8.        Discussion and possible action on a Resolution of the Town Council regarding the educational 
 specifications for the proposed new high school – Chairman Testa and Councilors Carmody,  
            Reynolds, Rivard, and Rossacci 
 
Town of Wallingford Town Council resolution concerning revisions to the educational specifications for 
the proposed high school consolidation project.  
 
Whereas the Wallingford Town Council recognizes the significance of the proposed high school 
consolidation project and its lasting impact on the students, educators, families, and taxpayers of the 
town of Wallingford. 
 
And whereas the educational specifications for the proposed project were developed through a process 
involving substantial public input including recommendations and advocacy from teachers, school staff, 
parents, students, and members of the community. 
 
And whereas the inclusion of 17 additional classrooms was strongly advocated for by teachers and 
school staff to provide each teacher with a dedicated classroom and to ensure an educational 
environment that best supports effective instruction, student learning and the daily operations of the 
school.  
 
And whereas teachers and school staff, whose professional experience and firsthand understanding of 
classroom needs are essential to the planning of educational facilities have consistently emphasized the 
importance of these additional classrooms.  
 
And whereas the inclusion of these 17 classrooms received support from a majority of the Board of 
Education at various stages of its deliberations and decision-making process.  
 
And whereas the town council is concerned that the subsequent revisions to the educational 
specifications eliminating the 17 classrooms represent a significant departure from the priorities 
established through public participation and the educational needs identified by teachers and school 
staff. 
 
And whereas the town council firmly believes that should the town proceed with the consolidation of its 
two high schools, the resulting facilities must reflect the highest standards of educational excellence and 
provide the best possible learning environment for current and future generations of Wallingford 
students.  
 
Now therefore, it be resolved that the Wallingford Town Council hereby formally expresses 
its opposition to the revisions to the educational specifications eliminating the 17 additional classrooms.

And be it further resolved that the town council strongly urges the Wallingford Board of Education to 
reconsider and reverse its decision and restore these classrooms to the educational specifications 
consistent with the recommendation of teachers, school staff, parents, students, and the substantial 
public input received throughout the planning process.  
 
And be it further resolved that the town council affirms its commitment to ensuring that any 
consolidation of the town's two high schools represents a responsible forward-looking investment in 
public education and provides the highest quality educational facilities reasonably achievable for the 
benefit of generations to come.  
 
Be it finally resolved that a copy of this resolution be transmitted to the Wallingford Board of Education 
for its formal consideration adopted by the Wallingford Town Council this 10th day of November, 2026.  
 
Councilor Rossacci spoke in support of the Resolution and feels the Board of Education should 
reconsider eliminating the 17 additional classrooms.   
 
Councilor Fishbein clarified that the Board of Education is a creature of the State of Connecticut.  The 
only connection to the Town of Wallingford is the budget.  We are essentially asking a state body to 
reconsider something that is already voted on.  He feels the teachers provided input and the teachers 
should be heard. If we are going to spend $400 million on a new high school, we should have the best 
high school available.   He offered some revisions to the Resolution. 
 
A question was asked how the Resolution was created.  Chairman Testa explained it was a caucus of the 
Democrats, having a discussion and jointly putting this item on the agenda.  Councilor Tatta asked a 
question about what documentation can be requested under the Freedom Of Information Act.  Attorney 
Small explained that communications regarding the Resolution could be requested under the Freedom of 
Information Act. Councilor Tatta stated she would like to have been included on the final draft of the 
resolution.  She is also concerned about the Board of Education re-voting on this issue and how the 
votes changed through the process.  She would like to know the reasons for the change. 
 
Councilor Reynolds spoke in support of the Resolution and feels we should not be making any changes 
to size or shape while we are in the process of negotiating to buy property.  We need to support our 
educators and plan smarter, think long term and think success. 
 
Councilor Rivard believes the best people to make the assessment for the schools are the professionals 
that work in them and supports the teachers getting the 17 classrooms.  If we are to move forward with 
this project we should do it right. 
 
Councilor Laffin explained that the 17 classrooms and the pool could affect our reimbursement rate.  He 
feels we should go to the State of Connecticut to lobby for that reimbursement to be covered.  He would 
like a real vote and this Resolution will not do anything to resolve the situation.  This is a Board decision 
and we need to follow the system the way is it designed.

Councilor Fishbein commented that before we can go to the State of Connecticut we need to find a site 
for the school. 
 
Chairman Testa feels the Board of Education made their decision to change the educational 
specifications based on a memo from the Mayor.  Mayor added that there is a possibility there are 
enough votes on Council to move forward with the project.  There is talk about the Council supporting a 
referendum for it.  If it goes to referendum and you get enough participation and positive votes, the 
project will move forward.  These are all variables.  Other variables include getting our legislative 
delegation to increase the reimbursement rate.  If we build the right size building, per pupil and square 
footage, the State of Connecticut could reimburse 52.5%.  The building we are trying to potentially build 
is looking at a reimbursement rate of 42.5%.  He feels we should absolutely be going to the State for 
more money but we cannot count on the certainty in the outcome.  He is hoping to get the most 
competitive 30-year term rate possible. 
 
Maureen Reed, Board of Education member spoke in support of the 17 classrooms.   She asked the 
Council to remember that every decision made in education should be about the kids.  She feels the 
Town Council needs to understand every aspect of the project as Council ultimately makes the decision 
about the land purchase and project.
